福爾摩沙小導遊臺南 Tainan・中西區

開基武廟Kaiji Martial Temple

認識全臺第一座關帝廟：從港邊草寮起家、靠商家香火撐起來的小關帝廟，以及藏在客廳大小空間裡的門釘、古鐘、匾額和虎爺。

Meet the little temple known as Taiwan's first Guandi temple: born in a grass hut, kept alive by merchants, and full of small treasures.

新美街上，夾在老街屋之間，有一座當地人叫作小關帝廟的小廟。文獻記載，鄭成功的部將從福建請來兩尊關公神像，起初供在港邊草寮。信眾越來越多，明鄭時期集資建廟，被視為全臺第一座關帝廟。來求籤的人太多，廟前的街被叫作抽籤巷；修廟的錢多由商家籌募。仔細看：門上是門釘不是門神，還有 1858 年的古鐘和「行大道」匾。正殿太小，虎爺住在馬使爺下方的壁龕。廟雖小，五臟俱全。

On Xinmei Street, squeezed between old shophouses, stands a small temple that locals call the Little Guandi Temple. Records say a general under Koxinga brought two Guan Gong statues from Fujian. At first, they stayed in a grass hut by the harbor. As worshippers grew, people built a real temple in the Zheng era. It is known as Taiwan's first Guandi temple. So many people came to draw fortune slips that the street was nicknamed Fortune-Slip Lane, and merchants paid for the repairs. Look closer: door studs instead of door gods, a bell from 1858, and plaques that say Follow the Great Way. The hall is so small that the Tiger Lord lives in a wall niche below the Horse Master. Small temple, full house.

一分鐘看懂

One-minute intro

為什麼值得來

Why it matters & history
  1. 小廟的身世大關帝廟是官方的；這座小廟，是百姓的。The big Martial Temple was the officials' temple. This little one belongs to the people.
  2. 看這裡！小廟裡的寶貝一座客廳大小的廟，裝著一整套人生課綱。A temple the size of a living room holds a whole lesson about life.
  3. 生意人的廟大關帝廟有官員參拜；小關帝廟，靠的是地方商家的香火。Officials prayed at the big temple. Local merchants kept this little one going.

認識景點

About the place

小廟的身世Where it all began

開基：就是開創；它被視為全臺第一座關帝廟。 從泉州來的神像：文獻記載，鄭成功的部將從福建泉州奉請兩尊關公神像來臺。 港邊草寮：神像起初供在港邊的草寮裡；信眾變多後才集資建廟。 永曆年間建廟：內政部資料記為明永曆 23 年（1669 年）建廟；也有資料說神像 1662 年左右來臺。

founding: Kaiji means founding. It is known as Taiwan's first Guandi temple. Statues from Quanzhou: Records say a general under Koxinga brought two Guan Gong statues from Quanzhou, Fujian. A grass hut by the harbor: At first the statues stayed in a grass hut. As worshippers grew, people raised money for a temple. Built in the Zheng era: Official records date the temple to 1669, in the Zheng era. Some sources say the statues arrived around 1662.

關帝港：當年船隻能駛進市區，廟靠近港口，所以又叫關帝港廟。 小關帝廟：比官方的祀典武廟小，當地人就叫它小關帝廟。

Guandi Port: Boats once sailed into the city. The temple stood near the harbor, so it is also called the Guandi Port Temple. The Little Guandi Temple: It is smaller than the official Martial Temple, so locals call it the Little Guandi Temple.

看這裡！小廟裡的寶貝Look closer: small treasures

門釘：1974 年起以門釘取代門神彩繪；門釘是高規格廟宇的象徵。 1858 年古鐘：正殿的古鐘鑄於清咸豐 8 年，鐘面有銘文。 衡文天闕：1776 年的「衡文天闕」匾，是廟中現存最古老的文物。 行大道：1806 年的匾，讚美關公走在正道上。

door studs: Since 1974 the doors have had studs instead of painted door gods. Studs mark a high-ranking temple. The 1858 bell: The bell in the main hall was cast in 1858 and has writing on it. The oldest plaque: The plaque Heng Wen Tian Que, from 1776, is the oldest object in the temple. Follow the Great Way: A plaque from 1806. It praises Guan Gong for following the Great Way.

立人極：1876 年的匾：為人立下最高的典範。 住錯地方的虎爺：虎爺通常住在神桌下；這裡空間太小，他和馬使爺、赤兔馬一起住在牆上的小龕，就在馬使爺的下方。

Set the highest example: A plaque from 1876. It means setting the highest example for people. The Tiger Lord's odd home: The Tiger Lord usually lives under the altar. Here the hall is so small that he lives in a wall niche, below the Horse Master and Red Hare.

生意人的廟The merchants' temple

抽籤巷：來求籤的人太多，廟前的街就被叫作抽籤巷。 商家出錢修廟：這是民間廟宇，歷來重修經費多由地方商家籌募。 侯雨利的起家厝：臺南幫的侯雨利來自北門，在廟旁買下店鋪兼住家，後來與王永慶並稱「南侯北王」。 戰火與重修：二戰末期廟宇受到戰火波及，戰後由地方人士集資修復。

Fortune-Slip Lane: So many people came to draw fortune slips that the street became Fortune-Slip Lane. Repairs paid by merchants: This was a people's temple. Local merchants paid for most of its repairs. Hou Yu-li's first home: Hou Yu-li of the Tainan Gang came from Beimen and bought a shop and home beside this temple. Later he and Wang Yung-ching were called Hou of the South, Wang of the North. War and repair: The temple was damaged near the end of World War Two. Local people raised money to repair it after the war.

新殿與舊殿：1976 年在後方蓋了新大殿，舊正殿保留下來作為歷史見證。 原正殿古蹟：1985 年「開基武廟原正殿」公告為古蹟，現為直轄市定古蹟。 憨番扛廟角：廟前屋角下，左右各有一個蹲著、好像扛著屋角的小人像，叫「憨番扛廟角」。相傳和荷蘭人統治臺灣的時代有關，也有人說它是守護廟宇的大力士。

New hall, old hall: In 1976 a new hall was built behind it, and the old main hall was kept as a record of history. A protected monument: In 1985 the old main hall was listed as a monument. Today it is a city monument. The roof-corner carriers: Under the front roof corners, two little crouching figures seem to carry the roof. People call them the foreigners carrying the temple corners. Stories about them differ.

實景照片

Photos on site

開基武廟正面 The Front Gate

廟門夾在兩棟樓房中間，屋頂上有彩色的龍。石柱上刻著對聯「漢代精忠耿耿日星並煥」「臺城肇祀巍巍宮闕重新」。左前方的石碑寫著「開基武廟正殿」，側面刻著「三級古蹟」。

The front gate is squeezed between two buildings. Colorful dragons stand on the roof. The stone post on the left marks the old main hall as a protected monument.

地上的石牌 The Stone in the Ground

門口地上的石牌寫著：本廟創建於明永曆二十三年（清康熙八年），也就是西元 1669 年。

A stone in the ground says the temple was founded in 1669.

憨番扛廟角 The Roof-Corner Carriers

抬頭看廟角：屋角下有兩個蹲著的小力士，左右各一個，好像在扛屋角，叫「憨番扛廟角」。關於它的說法不只一種：相傳和荷蘭人統治臺灣的時代有關，也有人說它是守護廟宇的大力士。屋脊上還有彩色的龍，中間是一顆火焰寶珠。

Look up at the roof corners! Two little crouching strongmen, one at each corner, seem to hold up the roof. People call them the foreigners carrying the temple corners. Stories differ: some link them to the time of Dutch rule, and others say they are strong temple guardians. Colorful dragons and a flaming pearl sit on the roof ridge.

龍門石雕 The Dragon Gate Carving

門邊的石雕：上面是雲浪中的龍，石頭上刻著「禹門」。禹門就是「龍門」，在黃河的峽谷裡，兩岸懸崖對峙、水流很急，相傳是大禹治水時開鑿的。傳說鯉魚逆流游到這裡，跳過去就會變成龍，比喻努力就能成功。下面刻的是吉祥的麒麟。

Beside the door is a stone dragon in clouds and waves. The carved words say Yu's Gate, another name for the Dragon Gate. It is a narrow gorge on the Yellow River with steep cliffs and fast water. Legend says Yu the Great cut it open to control the floods. A carp that swims up and jumps over it becomes a dragon, so it means hard work leads to success. Below is a qilin, a lucky animal.

馬使爺與虎爺 The Horse Master and the Tiger Lord

上面的小神龕寫著「馬使爺」，裡面有關公的馬和牽馬的馬使爺；正下方的拱形小龕住著虎爺。紅柱上寫著「土山三約當時漢賊已分明」，說的是《三國演義》裡，關公在土山和曹操約定三件事，表明他仍然忠於大哥劉備。

The small shrine says Horse Master. Inside are Guan Gong's horse and the Horse Master who leads it. Right below, the Tiger Lord sits in an arched niche. The red pillar recalls a story from the Romance of the Three Kingdoms. At Tushan, Guan Gong set three conditions and stayed loyal to his brother Liu Bei.

立人極匾 The Li Ren Ji Plaque

由右往左讀：「立人極」，意思是為人立下最高的榜樣。這是清光緒2年（1876年）的古匾，用來讚美關公。

Read it from right to left: Li Ren Ji. It means setting the highest example for people. This old plaque from 1876 praises Guan Gong.

行大道匾 The Xing Da Dao Plaque

由右往左讀：「行大道」，意思是走在正大光明的道路上。這是清嘉慶11年（1806年）的古匾，讚美關公。

Read it from right to left: Xing Da Dao. It means following the Great Way. This old plaque from 1806 praises Guan Gong.
